profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the algorithm lead and the systems lead for an ML research project implementing PSO-PS, a particle-swarm-based parameter synchronization method for distributed DNN training. The team is preparing a shared experimental package for an internal deadline: the algorithm side needs a clean set of synchronization-stage outputs and comparison tables, while the systems side needs to finalize the training harness, checkpoint conventions, and cluster run schedule. The agenda is to align on what gets handed off at each synchronization stage, which code/config version is the shared baseline, how results should be marked as 'reproduced,' and who maintains the canonical experiment manifest. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on interfaces, run ownership, and a Friday handoff for MNIST and CIFAR-10 experiments across several synchronization settings.

members.name: Dr. Lina Qureshi
members.expertise: Distributed optimization, swarm intelligence, convergence analysis for deep learning
members.background: Lina leads the algorithm workstream and adapted the PSO update rule to operate on worker-produced model states at synchronization boundaries; she typically works from research notebooks and small-scale validation runs before handing stabilized configs to engineering.
members.private_state: She wants the internal package to show the PSO aggregation behaving consistently across the paper's synchronization settings without reopening implementation debates, and she is worried that systems changes could blur whether deviations are algorithmic or infrastructural.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says 'sync every n mini-batches,' the count is global optimizer steps between PSO aggregation events, independent of each worker's local dataloader remainder behavior.
The 'baseline branch' means the research-frozen code snapshot used for the latest CIFAR-10 curves, even if the systems repo has newer launcher and logging changes.
A run is 'reproduced' once the main accuracy trend and relative ordering versus averaging are within normal random variation across one seeded run per setting.
The experiment manifest is conceptually owned by the algorithm side because it defines the paper-facing settings, while systems may mirror it for scheduling.

members.name: Evan Morales
members.role: ML Systems Engineer, Distributed Training Lead
members.expertise: PyTorch distributed systems, experiment orchestration, checkpointing and cluster execution
members.background: Evan owns the multi-GPU training harness and cluster submission pipeline; he focuses on making runs restartable, consistent across nodes, and easy to compare through a central manifest and dashboard.
members.private_state: He wants to standardize the PSO-PS experiments inside the existing training framework with minimal one-off handling, and he is concerned about ambiguous handoffs that create reruns or noncomparable logs close to the deadline.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'sync every n mini-batches,' they mean each worker performs n local mini-batches and then enters the synchronization barrier, which is what the launcher currently enforces.
The 'baseline branch' is the current mainline training harness with the recent checkpoint-resume and metric-logging fixes already merged.
A run is only 'reproduced' if the exact table entry can be regenerated from the tracked config with the expected artifacts, seed list, and summary metrics in the dashboard.
The canonical experiment manifest belongs to systems because scheduling, artifact paths, and restart behavior all depend on a single source of truth.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to running PSO-PS 'every 8 mini-batches' and 'using the same synchronization configuration as the paper.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means 8 optimizer steps between PSO aggregation stages as counted in the research code's logical training loop, effectively treating the synchronization interval as a global stage parameter.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means each worker executes 8 local mini-batches before entering a barrier and PSO aggregation, matching the distributed harness's worker-local counter.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase is standard and sounds fully specified; both believe the launcher already operationalizes the paper's setting, so neither thinks to unpack how the count is measured.

misalignment_points.topic: Which baseline code version is shared
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say they will 'use the baseline branch' and 'keep it aligned with the CIFAR-10 result we already have.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to a research snapshot branch cut two weeks earlier, the one used to generate the current comparison plots and containing a custom PSO logging patch.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the repository's current baseline/main branch, which includes newer resume semantics and standardized metric names but not Lina's exact snapshot state.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both sides assume there is one obvious baseline because each works from a branch they consider canonical, and the prior CIFAR-10 result functions as a vague shared reference rather than a pinned commit hash.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as a reproduced result
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'mark MNIST and CIFAR-10 as reproduced by Friday' before packaging the results.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes reproduction means obtaining the same qualitative trend and roughly similar final accuracy for PSO-PS versus averaging across the targeted synchronization settings, even from a single representative seed.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes reproduction means regenerating the tracked table entries from the standardized config set, including the expected seed bundle, artifact set, and dashboard summaries for each condition.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In research coordination, 'reproduced' usually signals success without forcing the exact standard into the conversation; each person assumes the other shares the norm from their own workflow.

misalignment_points.topic: Ownership and scope of the experiment manifest
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Evan will 'maintain the manifest' while Lina will 'finalize the settings.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes Evan will maintain only the execution-facing copy—paths, job names, and resource fields—while the authoritative list of experimental conditions and paper-facing labels remains hers.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes maintaining the manifest includes being the single owner of the canonical experiment specification, including condition names, seed lists, and which runs are considered official.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The split sounds complementary and reasonable on the surface, and 'manifest' naturally bundles both scientific settings and operational metadata without anyone noticing they draw the boundary differently.
